A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The original Appendices A–C match v2 Appendices E–G; the additional appendix material can be distinguished reliably from relocated content.

before.justification: Section 4.2 and Tables 1–4 report original synthetic-data experiments on mechanism-count recovery, EM convergence, and parameter-estimation errors.

after.justification: v2 retains the original synthetic-data experiments and their numerical results in Section 4.2 and Tables 1–4.

M1.justification: Definitions 1–2 revise the typing component to use pair-specific encoders receiving the full abstracted transition map, rather than only the target-variable transition function. This changes the formal model's encoder inputs, while the EM/LO-RANSAC recovery procedure and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same synthetic bivariate linear mechanisms with Laplacian noise and the same illustrative stress dynamical system. Appendix H's medical and economic applications are hypothetical discussions, not additional evaluated datasets or scenarios.

E2.justification: Neither version reports an evaluated external-baseline comparison. Newly discussed gating models, graph-switching systems, and PC/GES do not participate in the reported experiments; EM and LO-RANSAC remain components of the proposed approach.

E3.justification: The experiments retain 100 datasets per mechanism count, an average of 500 samples per class, the same class imbalances, 5 or 10 EM iterations, and the 0.2 parameter-acceptance threshold. The added statement excluding cyclic relations clarifies the existing procedure rather than documenting a protocol change.

E4.justification: The mechanism-count and class-imbalance analyses, convergence analysis, parameter-error analysis, and stress-system example are retained. New appendix discussions provide theoretical and applicability arguments rather than new ablations, robustness tests, or evaluated case studies.

E5.justification: Both versions report 500 randomly generated setups with 10 initializations each, the same 95% resampling-success target, and the same Anderson–Darling testing procedure. Run-count and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–4 are unchanged, including 14,859 theoretical versus 177 empirical resamples for four mechanisms and class deviation 0.2 in Table 2. The plotted examples and stress-system findings are also retained; no new empirical results are reported.

T1.justification: v2 revises the encoder definitions and conditioned-equation construction. New Appendix D introduces Definition 4 and Theorem D.1, with a proof that having only self-loop transitions is sufficient for reduction to a conditioned SCM; Appendix C adds functional-composition compatibility reasoning. The original sampling-bound derivation is retained in Appendix E.

C1.justification: The abstract and four listed contributions retain their scope. However, v2 removes the introductory qualification that classical causal perspectives might yield similar conclusions and explicitly says classical considerations cannot give the correct answer, strengthening the attribution claim.

C2.justification: v1 already discusses observational versus controlling interpretations. v2 substantially extends this treatment: Appendices B–D address identification choices and reduction boundaries, Appendix I explains why abstract types generally cannot be mapped back to data-generating equations, and Appendix H proposes mechanism-targeted health interventions and economic stability applications.

D1.justification: The stated code location changes from an anonymous 4open.science project to a named GitHub repository. Existing sampling parameters, optimization settings, and pseudocode are retained, including the sampling instructions moved from Appendix C to Appendix G.

R1.justification: A new Gating Models paragraph relates the framework to Minka and Winn, Winn, and Liu et al.'s graph-switching dynamical systems. Additional citations address causal emergence and identification. The existing transportability, reinforcement-learning, language-model, and actual-causality positioning remains largely intact.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the introduction, formalism explanations, stress discussion, and conclusion while retaining the six-section main narrative. It expands the appendix organization around the relocated original material and updates author information, acknowledgments, and conference headers.

P2.justification: Table 2 is reformatted with separate class-deviation and analysis-type columns, and Figure 2's caption is revised. Tables 3 and 4 move from a shared appendix page to separate placements. The same three figures and four tables remain, without new graphical results.

improvement.justification: The explicit reducibility definition and sufficient criterion, together with clearer identification and generative limitations in Appendices B, D, and I, make the central framework easier to assess. These gains are tempered by the conclusion's stronger assertion of proved expressiveness beyond conventional SCMs, which the sufficient reduction theorem alone does not establish.
